children: Nobility Homes reported third-quarter fiscal 2026 results with revenue of $12.14 million, net income of $1.90 million and diluted EPS of $0.60 for the quarter ended August 1, 2026. For the first nine months of fiscal 2026 the company reported sales of $35.05 million and net income of $5.28 million (diluted EPS $1.66). Management highlighted a strong balance sheet with cash, certificates of deposit and short-term investments totaling $25.8 million and no outstanding debt.
Net income (three months ended August 1, 2026): $1,896,342; Diluted EPS: $0.60.
Nine months ended August 1, 2026 — Sales: $35,051,636; Net income: $5,284,095; Diluted EPS: $1.66.

Sales mix shift: fewer new retail homes sold in company-owned retail centers (137 vs. 195 year-over-year) while sales to independent dealers increased (184 vs. 129), with dealer sales carrying lower margins.
Management cited continued buyer hesitation and a shift toward lower-cost homes amid higher interest rates and economic uncertainty, weighing on demand.
Operational challenges include supplier delays, back orders, material price increases, tariffs and labor shortages that have slowed completion of homes at the manufacturing facility.
Company noted ongoing inflation in several building products and expects these supply-chain and cost pressures to persist through fiscal 2026 into 2027.
Corporate milestones: celebrated 59 years in business and emphasized long-standing retail presence in Florida and vertical integration including an insurance agency subsidiary.
